prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need, how much hand‑holding you want, and whether you prefer a local agent or an online broker. A few quick options and the best way to choose:

What to decide first
- Type of coverage: ACA individual/family plan, short‑term, small‑group for a sole proprietor with employees, Medicare, dental, or ancillary coverage?  
- Do you want in‑person, phone, or entirely online help?
- Are you eligible for premium tax credits (subsidies) through the Marketplace?

Where to look
- Local independent agents/independent agencies in Kansas City that work with multiple carriers — best for tailored shopping and plan network checks. (Local agents can compare many insurers and often help year‑round.)
- Online brokers/marketplaces (HealthSherpa, eHealth) — convenient for quotes and Marketplace enrollments.
- Healthcare.gov broker/assister finder — if you want someone certified to enroll you in Marketplace plans and subsidies.
- Missouri Department of Insurance — to verify a broker’s license and complaint history.

How to evaluate a broker (quick checklist)
- Licensed in Missouri and appointed with multiple carriers (ask which ones).
- Experience with self‑employed clients and Marketplace/subsidy rules.
- Transparent about fees/commissions (some brokers charge no fee; others charge a service fee).
- Will compare multiple plans, check provider network and pharmacy coverage, and explain HSA eligibility and estimated out‑of‑pocket costs.
- Responsive, good reviews, and willing to support you year‑round (not just at enrollment).

Questions to ask when you interview a broker
- Do you work with individual Marketplace plans and private plans? Which carriers do you represent?  
- Do you charge a fee for your services?  
- How will you determine whether I qualify for premium tax credits?  
- Will you check provider and drug coverage for my doctors and medications?  
- How long have you worked with self‑employed clients?

If you want specific names
Tell me your ZIP code and whether you want in‑person help or are okay with online, and I’ll pull up a few licensed independent brokers/agents in the Kansas City, MO area with good reviews and the right specialties (individual/sole‑proprietor).
